name: Pancreatic cystic neoplasm
lead: Which cyst this is, whether any feature of it crosses a resection threshold, and — because four guidelines give four different answers on intervals, thresholds and stopping — which answer this programme has actually agreed to work to.
gatelabel: The decision in front of you

gates.name: 1 · What kind of cyst is this?
crit: MRI with MRCP, or pancreas-protocol CT where MRI is contraindicated, reviewed with the cyst's relation to the main duct established
Main pancreatic duct diameter recorded in millimetres, not as the word 'dilated'
History of pancreatitis, alcohol or trauma taken — a pseudocyst does not belong on an oncological pathway
Septation, mural nodule with its height in millimetres, wall calcification, central scar, solid component and location all recorded
Whether a prior study exists, on which modality, and over what interval
gates.ask: Am I looking at an IPMN, and if so does it involve the main duct — because every later gate turns on that one answer?

standard.t: Characterise the cyst on MRI with MRCP and write the main pancreatic duct diameter down in millimetres, because the 5 mm and 10 mm duct thresholds are what separate surveillance from an operation.
standard.pref: Every incidental or symptomatic pancreatic cyst at first presentation. ACG names MRCP the preferred modality for pancreatic cyst surveillance; Kyoto 2024 builds its whole algorithm on duct diameter and on the height and enhancement of a mural nodule, so a report that omits those measurements cannot be acted on. Reported accuracy for naming the cyst type is 40 to 50% for MRI, CT and EUS without aspiration per ACG and 40 to 95% for MRI and 40 to 81% for CT per the European guideline; for benign against malignant, 55 to 76%.
standard.avoid: Do not accept a report that says 'cystic lesion of the pancreas, recommend follow-up' with no duct diameter, no nodule height and no comment on communication with the duct. That report cannot be placed anywhere on this page.
standard.note: Duct communication is the single most useful discriminator in practice but is not by itself diagnostic: a mucinous cystic neoplasm does not communicate, a branch-duct IPMN does, and both are mucinous. Kyoto 2024 is explicit that the classification of mixed IPMN remains ambiguous between imaging and pathology definitions and left the categories unchanged. The measurements are what this gate asks for; the thresholds applied to them are consensus lines and are argued at gate 2.

opts.name: Main-duct IPMN
opts.when: Segmental or diffuse dilatation of the main pancreatic duct of 5 mm or more without an obstructing cause. Kyoto 2024 makes a duct of 10 mm or more a high-risk stigma and a duct of 5 to 9 mm a worrisome feature. The 5 mm definition is Fukuoka 2012's, lowered from the 10 mm used at Sendai in 2006 to raise radiological sensitivity, and Fukuoka 2012 cited no study comparing outcomes above and below the new line.
opts.pref: Treat as a surgical disease until proved otherwise. Kyoto 2024 reports mean rates in resected main-duct specimens of 62% (range 36 to 100%) for high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma and 43% (11 to 81%) for invasive carcinoma alone. Fukuoka 2012 pooled 3,568 resected IPMNs and reported more than 62.2% and 43.6% for the main-duct subset; Sendai 2006 pooled nine smaller resected series and reported 70% (57 to 92%) and 43% (23 to 57%). NCCN quotes about 62% and recommends resection in operable patients with a main-duct IPMN of 10 mm or more.
opts.avoid: Every one of those percentages is the prevalence of malignancy in specimens that were taken out, so they describe the yield of past operating decisions and not the risk in the cyst in front of you. Four guideline generations have carried them forward without supplying a denominator: Sendai 2006 made the recommendation to resect all main-duct IPMN with no data at all on what happens to an unresected one, and there are still none. Do not quote 62% to a patient in clinic as their personal risk.

opts.name: Branch-duct IPMN
opts.when: Cystic dilatation of side branches of more than 5 mm communicating with a non-dilated main duct. The commonest incidental finding — Kyoto 2024 puts about 80% of incidentally discovered cysts in this category — and the population every surveillance schedule on this page was written for.
opts.pref: Risk-stratify rather than operate. Resected-series rates in Kyoto 2024 are 31% (15 to 48%) for high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma and 19% (6 to 38%) for invasive carcinoma, and Kyoto 2024 now adds, in the same paragraph, that given the large number of unresected indolent branch-duct lesions the real rate across all branch-duct IPMNs is much lower — without saying how much lower, or supplying the denominator that would make the figure usable. In surveillance cohorts the numbers are an order of magnitude smaller: in 1,404 branch-duct IPMNs followed at the University of Tokyo the cumulative incidence of pancreatic carcinoma was 3.3% at 5 years, 6.6% at 10 and 15.0% at 15, an annual rate of about 0.7%.
opts.avoid: Do not read 'branch duct' as 'benign', and do not read the Tokyo figures as an unselected natural history either: that cohort excluded any lesion with a mural nodule or a duct of 10 mm or more at diagnosis, and anyone diagnosed with carcinoma or resected within 6 months, which strips prevalent disease out of the numerator while keeping its risk factors in the denominator. Within it, 30 of 68 carcinomas were concomitant ductal adenocarcinoma arising elsewhere in the gland, and cyst size and duct diameter predicted the IPMN-derived cancers (subdistribution hazard ratio 1.85 per 10 mm, 95% CI 1.38 to 2.48) but not the concomitant ones (P=.60) — so watching the cyst does not watch the whole pancreas.

opts.name: Mixed-type IPMN
opts.when: Both a dilated main duct and communicating branch-duct cysts. Kyoto 2024 states plainly that it is difficult to assign significance to this category and left it unchanged from 2017.
opts.pref: Manage by its highest-risk component — in practice as a main-duct IPMN, which is what the European guideline recommends at GRADE 2C on the ground that mixed-type carries comparable risk. That is the convention, not a result.
opts.avoid: Do not use the label to split the difference between surveillance and resection. There is no interval schedule and no resection threshold specific to mixed-type disease in any of the four guidelines. The category is also an artefact of a definition change nobody followed through: Fukuoka 2012 lowered the main-duct threshold to more than 5 mm, which enlarged the mixed group, recorded that enlargement as a classification problem, and never addressed what it meant for management.

standard.order: Ordered by malignant potential as the guidelines describe it, from the resected-series rates in Kyoto 2024. Those rates are prevalences in operated specimens and Kyoto 2024 says so; no trial compares management by subtype, and the order reflects guideline wording and the composition of past surgical series only.
standard.flagnote: Ratification item: how this programme classifies a main pancreatic duct of 5 to 9 mm with branch-duct cysts — main-duct, mixed, or branch-duct with a worrisome feature. Kyoto 2024 declines to resolve it, the three labels carry three different surveillance intervals, and a duct of 5 to 9 mm is simultaneously the definition of main-duct disease and a feature the same guideline says should be observed rather than resected. The European guideline goes further and makes a duct of more than 5 mm a resection threshold, at GRADE 2C and with only weak agreement among its own panel. Leaving this unstated means the same patient gets different follow-up depending on who reports the scan. Audit: subtype assigned at first board, duct diameter, interval given.

standard.t: Say out loud how confident the imaging diagnosis actually is, because it is wrong often enough to change the conversation.
standard.pref: Every cyst discussed at the board. In 115 consecutive pancreatic cyst resections in Amsterdam the preoperative diagnosis was correct in 83 (72.2%), and the simpler benign-versus-premalignant distinction in 99 (86.1%). Accuracy was not uniform: 89.0% for main-duct or mixed IPMN and 80.0% for side-branch IPMN, but 33.3% for serous cystic neoplasm, 33.3% for neuroendocrine tumour, 50.0% for solid pseudopapillary neoplasm and 0% for lymphoepithelial cysts, lymphangiomas, retention cysts and fluid collections.
standard.avoid: Do not build a ten-year surveillance commitment on a diagnosis you would not put in writing. Incidental cysts are also extremely common: on population MRCP in 1,077 German adults the weighted prevalence of a cyst of 2 mm or more was 49.1%, with a further weighted 12.9% five-year incidence of new cysts, and no cyst carrier died of pancreatic disease in a mean 5.9 years.
standard.note: Read that prevalence with its construction. 49.1% is a reweighted estimate; the observed proportion was 494 of 1,077 (45.9%), the MRI response rate was 54.7% within a cohort already attrited from 4,310 to 2,333, and the threshold counted any T2-hyperintense focus of 2 mm or more. Of the 494 carriers, 23 (5.1%) had a largest cyst of 10 to 20 mm and 3 (0.7%) one above 20 mm — 26 of 1,077 participants, 2.4% — which is the only part of that population any of these guidelines was written about. Three SHIP participants died of pancreatic cancer and two of the three had declined the MRI, so the only potentially informative cases are missing from the imaging cohort.

alt.t: Add endoscopic ultrasound where the main-duct diameter or a mural nodule cannot be settled on cross-sectional imaging.
alt.pref: Kyoto 2024 recommends EUS, including contrast-enhanced EUS and EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration, where high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma is suspected and the service is available, and names EUS the modality for confirming a mural nodule and measuring its height. ACG also accepts EUS as the primary surveillance tool where MRI is unavailable. The European guideline reports EUS morphology alone at 36 to 91% sensitivity and 45 to 81% specificity with accuracy 48 to 94%, and recommends contrast-harmonic EUS for nodules specifically.
alt.avoid: Not a routine first test for every incidental small cyst. Kyoto 2024 says aspiration should not be performed when a high-risk stigma is already obvious on CT or MRI and surgery will follow whatever the result; the European guideline says the same and adds that EUS-FNA should be done only when the result is expected to change management.
alt.note: Kyoto 2024's main structural change from Fukuoka 2017 is that EUS findings and EUS-FNA cytology are now inside the definitions of high-risk stigmata and worrisome features rather than sitting outside the algorithm. The same document states that EUS diagnostic ability is highly operator-dependent and cannot be delivered to the same standard everywhere, and puts the overall sensitivity of EUS-FNA cyst fluid cytology at 28.7% (range 4.8 to 61.5%). So the test now carries an absolute surgical indication when positive and almost no weight when negative, and Kyoto never states that asymmetry. [EXPERTISE]

alt.t: Pancreas-protocol CT is an acceptable substitute where MRI is contraindicated or unavailable, provided the duct is measurable.
alt.pref: Pacemaker, severe claustrophobia, renal contraindication to gadolinium, or no MRI access. Fukuoka 2017 and Kyoto 2024 both write their surveillance intervals as CT or MRI.
alt.avoid: Avoid repeated CT as the long-term surveillance modality in a young patient committed to decades of imaging — ACG prefers MRCP, and the cumulative radiation argument has no outcome data behind it but is the reason the preference exists.
alt.note: Whatever modality is chosen, keep it the same: a size change between a CT and an MRI is not reliably a size change.

avoid.t: Do not call a cyst a pseudocyst on imaging alone in a patient with no pancreatitis history.
avoid.pref: Where the question is genuinely open, cyst fluid amylase below 250 U/L effectively excludes a pseudocyst — pooled sensitivity 44% and specificity 98% across 12 studies, with amylase values available in 155 of the 450 pooled patients. The European guideline quotes the same two figures.
avoid.avoid: The error is consequential in one direction: a mucinous neoplasm managed as a pseudocyst may be drained, stented or ignored for years, and in one series of 134 symptomatic cysts 44% of those presenting with pancreatitis and a neoplastic cyst were initially called pseudocysts. Low sensitivity means a high amylase does not make it a pseudocyst either.
avoid.note: That pooled analysis explicitly excluded IPMN, which is now the commonest neoplastic pancreatic cyst and the subject of most of this page, so its figures were never derived in the population they are being applied to. The 250 U/L line was chosen to maximise correct classification within the same pooled data that report its performance, and in two contributing studies pseudocysts were diagnosed from a pancreatitis history plus follow-up rather than pathology, which inflates specificity for the mucinous arm. Use it as a rule-in test for a collection and nothing else.

avoid.t: Do not enter a cyst into surveillance without a baseline measurement, a named subtype and a recorded duct diameter.
avoid.pref: One board entry at the start, with size, subtype, duct diameter, nodule height, modality and the interval chosen, so that the word 'stable' three years later means something.
avoid.avoid: Growth is a worrisome feature in Kyoto 2024 at 2.5 mm per year, a high-risk characteristic in ACG at more than 3 mm per year, a worrisome feature in Fukuoka 2017 at 5 mm over 2 years and a relative indication for surgery in the European guideline at 5 mm per year. None of the four can be applied to a cyst whose baseline was never measured on a comparable study, and in practice that is the commonest reason a surveillance programme cannot act on its own data.
avoid.note: Grade D: this is an operational requirement, not a result. It is also the only way the growth thresholds become auditable, and none of the four has published measurement reproducibility.

gates.name: 2 · High-risk stigmata — this one leaves surveillance
crit: Obstructive jaundice in a patient with a cystic lesion of the head of the pancreas
Enhancing mural nodule of 5 mm or more, or a solid component
Main pancreatic duct of 10 mm or more
Cytology suspicious or positive for high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma, where cytology was obtained
gates.ask: Is there a feature here that takes this decision out of surveillance altogether, and is this patient fit for what that means?

standard.t: Resect, in a patient fit for pancreatectomy, for jaundice with a head cyst, an enhancing mural nodule of 5 mm or more or a solid component, a main pancreatic duct of 10 mm or more, or cytology suspicious or positive for high-grade dysplasia or carcinoma.
standard.pref: This is the Kyoto 2024 high-risk stigmata list, and the European 2018 absolute indications for surgery are almost the same four, at GRADE 1B. The list does separate risk. In a 3,336-patient cohort at the University of Tokyo, pancreatic carcinoma was diagnosed within 6 months in 49% of IPMNs with a high-risk stigma, against 1.3% with worrisome features only and 0.05% with no risk factor, and the individual stigmata carried multivariable odds ratios of 20.7 (95% CI 10.9 to 39.4) for a mural nodule of 5 mm or more, 14.6 (6.94 to 30.6) for a duct of 10 mm or more and 69.0 (17.0 to 280) for suspicious or positive cytology; all 7 patients with obstructive jaundice had carcinoma, so no odds ratio could be computed.
standard.avoid: Read that 49% as what it is. It is a prevalence at the moment the stigma was found, in a study where the stigma is itself what triggered the work-up that found the cancer, so the figure measures how well the criteria select patients for investigation and not how well they predict future disease; nothing in the design separates the two. The reported odds ratio of 2,269 for high-risk stigmata overall is a separation artefact — one event among 2,189 patients in the reference stratum — and should not be quoted as an effect size. A high-risk stigma is also not a diagnosis: Kyoto 2024 says high-risk stigmata do not have perfect specificity and that the operative decision must weigh general condition, comorbidity, life expectancy and patient preference. In a non-operated multicentre cohort of 281 patients, 5-year disease-specific survival with a high-risk stigma was 60.2% — a real risk of IPMN-related death, but not 100% — falling to 0% with two or more stigmata against 82.1% with one.
standard.note: The 5 mm nodule threshold is a measurement on EUS or on contrast-enhanced cross-sectional imaging of an enhancing nodule; a non-enhancing mucin globule is not a mural nodule and is the commonest false positive, which is why Kyoto and the European guideline both name contrast-enhanced EUS for this. The threshold itself is a convention: Fukuoka 2017 reported that nodule heights of 5, 7 and 10 mm all predicted high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma similarly (sensitivity 73 to 100%, specificity 73 to 85%) and chose 5 mm by expert agreement, and Kyoto 2024 considered moving to 10 mm, recorded that one EUS analysis gave a 10 mm nodule an odds ratio of 7.90 with a 67% probability of high-grade dysplasia or carcinoma against 2.93 and under 19% for a nodule of 5 to 10 mm, and kept 5 mm anyway for lack of evidence strongly supporting the change. That is an approvals item.

standard.t: Treat a main-duct IPMN with a duct of 10 mm or more as a resection problem rather than a surveillance problem.
standard.pref: A fit patient with segmental or diffuse main-duct dilatation of 10 mm or more. NCCN states that the international group strongly recommends resection in patients who can undergo surgery with main-duct IPMNs of 10 mm or more, and the European guideline lists a duct of 10 mm or more among its absolute indications. In the Tokyo cohort a duct of 10 mm or more carried a multivariable odds ratio of 14.6 (95% CI 6.94 to 30.6) for carcinoma found within 6 months.
standard.avoid: Do not present 10 mm as a derived threshold. Kyoto 2024 reports that a duct of 10 mm or more alone carries an odds ratio of only 1.06 to 1.76 in recent multivariable nomogram models, and the European guideline sets its own resection threshold at more than 5 mm — a position that reached only weak agreement among its own panel, at GRADE 2C, on the strength of resected series reporting high-grade dysplasia or malignancy in 91% at 6 mm or more (n=61), 30% at 6 mm or more (n=204), 56% at 8 mm or more (n=52), 59% at 5 mm or more (n=320) and 49% at 5 mm or more (n=158). Five, six and ten millimetres are three live thresholds derived from the composition of past operations.
standard.note: Downgraded to D from C after the full-text read: the recommendation is a consensus line that Kyoto 2024's own commissioned evidence does not support at that value, and the figures on either side of it are prevalences in resected specimens. Rule out an obstructing carcinoma or chronic pancreatitis as the cause of the dilated duct first — a duct dilated because something is blocking it is a different disease and, if it is adenocarcinoma, this is the PDAC pathway from here. Do not extrapolate from the duct to the whole gland: a long segment of duct involvement raises the question of total pancreatectomy, which Kyoto 2024 declines to recommend prophylactically, so see gate 7 before committing to an extent.

opts.name: Straight to resection without aspiration
opts.when: Kyoto 2024: EUS-FNA for cytology and molecular markers 'should not be performed when HRS is obvious in MDCT/MRI, and therefore surgery will be done regardless of the result'. The European guideline agrees at GRADE 2C: do not aspirate when the diagnosis is established or there is a clear indication for surgery.
opts.pref: An unambiguous high-risk stigma in a fit patient at a high-volume centre. The aspirate cannot lower the risk enough to cancel the operation, and it adds a procedure, a delay and a small pancreatitis risk.
opts.avoid: Not where the entity itself is in doubt — a serous cystadenoma with a central scar, a cystic neuroendocrine tumour or a walled-off collection can all be mistaken for a solid component, preoperative diagnosis was wrong in 32 of 115 resections (28%), and serous and neuroendocrine lesions were correctly called before the operation only a third of the time.

opts.name: EUS with aspiration first
opts.when: Kyoto 2024 recommends EUS, including contrast-enhanced EUS and FNA, in IPMN suspected of harbouring high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma where the service is available, and now counts the cytology result as a high-risk stigma in its own right: by the WHO definition the absolute risk of high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma is 91 to 100% for a 'suspicious' and 100% for a 'positive' result.
opts.pref: Where the diagnosis rather than the risk is the question, where cytology would change the extent of the operation, or where a frail patient's willingness to proceed depends on how certain the diagnosis is.
opts.avoid: Do not use a negative aspirate to reverse a decision made on a high-risk stigma: Kyoto 2024's own pooled sensitivity for cyst fluid cytology is 28.7% (range 4.8 to 61.5%), so a negative result carries almost no information. The seeding risk, which Fukuoka 2012 treated as a reason not to aspirate at all, is now quantified rather than asserted: Kyoto 2024 reports needle-tract seeding in 0.3% of pancreatic cystic lesions by systematic review and peritoneal seeding in 2.3% of resected IPMNs that had preoperative EUS-FNA against 4.4% of those that did not (P=0.403), with every seeded IPMN proving high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma on pathology; the European guideline reports adverse events in 44 of 1,313 aspirations (3.4%), of which 1 was severe.

alt.order: Ordered as Kyoto 2024 orders it — operate without aspirating when the stigma is obvious — not because any study compares the two strategies. None does.
alt.flagnote: Ratification item: whether this programme requires EUS before every cyst resection. ACG and Kyoto both make EUS conditional on the clinical question; the practical choice is between a standard pre-resection EUS, which costs a procedure in every case, and a selective one, which accepts that some resections will be done on cross-sectional imaging alone in a disease where one preoperative diagnosis in four is wrong. Decide separately who reads the cytology and whether a local 'suspicious' result is treated as an absolute indication, since that is what Kyoto 2024 now makes it. Audit: proportion of cyst resections with preoperative EUS, cytology result, and the final histology in each.

avoid.t: Do not treat a cyst of 30 mm or more as a high-risk stigma. It is a worrisome feature, and it has been one since 2012.
avoid.pref: Count it with the other worrisome features at gate 3 and let the count, not the number, drive the next step.
avoid.avoid: Sendai 2006 treated a branch-duct cyst of more than 30 mm as a resection trigger, on multivariate analyses in two Japanese series of 15 and 32 patients, and said in its own text that more pathological data were needed before all such lesions were resected. Fukuoka 2012 moved it to a worrisome feature on the stated ground that size above 3 cm is a weaker indicator of malignancy than mural nodules or positive cytology; Fukuoka 2017 went further and said that size alone is not an appropriate parameter to indicate surgery given its poor predictive value, while keeping 3 cm as a worrisome feature and 2 cm as a consideration under age 65; and Kyoto 2024 keeps it as a worrisome feature. In the Tokyo validation cohort a single worrisome feature of any kind carried a subdistribution hazard ratio for later pancreatic cancer of 1.43 (95% CI 0.93 to 2.19), which is not significant.
avoid.note: The size thresholds have validation evidence against them, not just absent evidence for them. In the same 3,336-patient cohort, long-term risk was stratified at 20 mm but not at 30 mm: the subdistribution hazard ratio was 2.07 (95% CI 1.38 to 3.10) for a cyst of 20 to 29 mm and 1.75 (1.00 to 3.08) for one of 30 mm or more, against under 20 mm. The authors attribute this to an unvalidated cut-off; it is also a failure of the criterion the study set out to validate, and 30 mm is the line Kyoto uses to set its shortest surveillance interval. The European guideline is the outlier in the other direction: a cyst of 40 mm or more is one of its relative indications for surgery, adopted with no head-to-head comparison and alongside its own text reporting that a cyst of 30 mm or more without other risk factors has a positive predictive value of 27 to 33%. Thirty, forty and 'not on its own' are three live positions, which is why this is an approvals item.

avoid.t: Do not let a high-risk stigma override an honest assessment of whether this patient survives a pancreatectomy.
avoid.pref: Gate 6 is the fitness gate and it is deliberately downstream of this one. Kyoto 2024 requires general condition, comorbidity, life expectancy and preference to be weighed in every operative decision.
avoid.avoid: An operation driven by a threshold in a patient who will not benefit from it is the characteristic failure mode of this disease, and it is not corrected by the threshold being correct. The numbers to weigh against the threshold are not in the guidelines that set it: Sendai 2006, Fukuoka 2012, Fukuoka 2017 and Kyoto 2024 quantify surgical mortality and morbidity nowhere at all, and neither does the European guideline. AGA 2015 and ACG 2018 do — AGA cites 2% postoperative mortality with 30% major morbidity in centres of excellence against 6.6% across all US pancreatic surgery in SEER, and ACG cites 2.1% mortality and 30% morbidity for cyst resection.
avoid.note: Grade D: this is a logical requirement rather than a comparative result. It is also where the page departs from its own spine, because Kyoto 2024 asks for life expectancy to be weighed without ever stating what the operation costs.

gates.name: 3 · Worrisome features — count them, then do EUS
crit: Cyst of 30 mm or more, or growth of 2.5 mm per year or faster
Enhancing mural nodule under 5 mm, or thickened or enhancing cyst walls
Main pancreatic duct 5 to 9 mm, or an abrupt change in duct calibre with distal atrophy
Acute pancreatitis, new-onset or worsening diabetes, or a raised serum CA 19-9
Regional lymphadenopathy
gates.ask: How many worrisome features does this patient actually have, and what does EUS change about what I do next?

standard.t: Count the worrisome features rather than reacting to one, because the number carries more risk than any single feature.
standard.pref: Every cyst without a high-risk stigma. In the 3,336-patient Tokyo cohort the subdistribution hazard ratio for later pancreatic cancer rose with the count: 1.43 (95% CI 0.93 to 2.19) with one feature, 2.17 (1.17 to 4.05) with two, and 10.1 (4.20 to 24.5) with three or four, against none. Kyoto 2024 states that multiple worrisome features have an additive effect.
standard.avoid: Do not convert the count into a score and then into an operation. Kyoto 2024 notes that the published nomograms have limitations — several do not distinguish branch-duct from main-duct disease, resected numbers are small in some regions and external validation is absent — and declines to endorse one, so the count informs how hard to look, not whether to operate. The single study Kyoto cites for additivity reports risk of high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma rising to 22%, 34% and 59% with one, two and three features and reaching 100% with four or more, with no sample sizes and no confidence intervals given; a 100% rate is the kind of small-cell result that does not survive replication.
standard.note: Individually, the three worrisome features that carried independent long-term risk in that cohort were a main duct of 5 to 9.9 mm (SHR 3.46, 2.04 to 5.89), acute pancreatitis (5.65, 1.86 to 17.2) and a growth rate of 2.5 mm per year or more (3.83, 2.14 to 6.86); the others did not reach significance on their own. Three limits on the gradient matter at the bedside. It was measured in a cohort from which every patient with a high-risk stigma, and everyone diagnosed with carcinoma or resected within 6 months, had been removed. Half the events were concomitant ductal adenocarcinoma arising elsewhere in the gland (68 of 138), and the gradient holds only for the IPMN-derived cancers (P for heterogeneity .002) — for two to four features the SHR was 6.25 (3.29 to 11.9) for derived carcinoma and non-significant for concomitant. And among patients who already had a high-risk stigma, the number of worrisome features predicted nothing (P for trend .50).

standard.t: Do endoscopic ultrasound, with contrast enhancement where available, when worrisome features raise the question of high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma.
standard.pref: The patient with worrisome features in whom the next step is genuinely open. Kyoto 2024's central structural change is that EUS findings and EUS-FNA cytology are now part of the assessment of high-risk stigmata and worrisome features, so the question EUS answers is whether this patient is in fact a gate 2 patient. EUS is the modality Kyoto names for confirming a mural nodule and measuring its height.
standard.avoid: Do not do EUS as a reflex on a small stable cyst with one soft feature. ACG restricts EUS with or without FNA to cysts with the features listed in gate 2 plus a cyst of 3 cm or more, jaundice, cyst-related acute pancreatitis, a significantly raised serum CA 19-9, or a main duct over 5 mm.
standard.note: ACG's main-duct trigger for EUS or multidisciplinary referral is over 5 mm, which is the same number Kyoto uses to open its worrisome-feature band. The two guidelines agree on this threshold and disagree about almost every interval. Kyoto also records that EUS cannot be delivered to the same standard in every service and that its diagnostic ability is highly operator-dependent, and the European guideline reports considerable interobserver variation in EUS-based diagnosis — so what EUS adds here depends on who does it. [EXPERTISE]

standard.t: Define growth rate before using it, because the four guidelines that use growth define it four different ways and none derived its threshold.
standard.pref: Kyoto 2024 uses a cystic growth rate of 2.5 mm per year or more as a worrisome feature, and that value has supporting data as a risk factor: subdistribution hazard ratio 3.83 (95% CI 2.14 to 6.86) for later pancreatic cancer. ACG makes growth of more than 3 mm per year a high-risk characteristic prompting a short-interval study. Fukuoka 2017 used an increase of 5 mm or more over 2 years. The European guideline uses 5 mm per year or more as a relative indication for surgery.
standard.avoid: Do not present any of the four as derived. Kyoto 2024 states that reported predictive growth rates range from 0.96 to 3.5 mm per year and that it adopted 2.5 because that was the value reported most frequently — a choice by vote frequency among candidate numbers, not by performance. Fukuoka 2017's 5 mm over 2 years entered on two citations. ACG's 3 mm per year is given with no operating characteristics, and the AGA technical review it otherwise draws on had found that an increase in cyst size was not a statistically significant risk factor for malignancy at all. And do not apply any of them across different modalities, slice thicknesses or readers: none of the four has published measurement reproducibility, and 2.5 mm is within the range over which two radiologists reading the same cyst can disagree.
standard.note: Downgraded to D from C after the full-text read: the threshold is a consensus value selected by frequency of publication, not a derived cut-off, however well the resulting variable performs in one cohort. There is also a signal the guidelines do not use. In the 804 Tokyo patients followed beyond 5 years, the increase in main pancreatic duct diameter over the first 5 years predicted later carcinoma (SHR 1.71 per mm, 1.44 to 2.03) while the increase in cyst size did not (1.46, 0.96 to 2.20) — and Kyoto 2024 considered adding 'increase in size of MPD' as a worrisome feature and rejected it for lack of evidence. Median duct increase over those 5 years was 0.2 mm (range −2.0 to 9.0), so this is a measurement that demands a consistent protocol. Whether this programme records duct growth as well as cyst growth is an approvals item.

opts.name: EUS-FNA of cyst fluid
opts.when: The established adjunct, recommended by Kyoto 2024 where high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma is suspected, by ACG for the trigger features above, by the European guideline at GRADE 2C only when the result is expected to change management, and by AGA 2015 only when at least two of three high-risk features are present.
opts.pref: Where fluid chemistry, cytology or molecular testing will change the plan — see gate 4 for which test answers which question.
opts.avoid: Do not aspirate a cyst too small to yield fluid, and do not aspirate when the result cannot change management. The procedural risk is now quantified rather than asserted: adverse events in 44 of 1,313 aspirations (3.4%) in the European guideline's pooled series, 34 mild, 9 moderate and 1 severe; needle-tract seeding in 0.3% of pancreatic cystic lesions and peritoneal seeding in 2.3% of resected IPMNs with preoperative FNA against 4.4% without (P=0.403) in Kyoto 2024.

opts.name: Through-the-needle microforceps biopsy
opts.when: A microforceps passed through a 19-gauge FNA needle to take a wall biopsy. Not recommended by any of the four guidelines as standard; ACG states there are no published data for this indication. An option at centres that do it.
opts.pref: The cyst whose type remains unresolved after fluid analysis, where an ovarian-type stroma or a serous epithelium would end the discussion. In 11 studies and 518 patients, pooled technical success was 97.1% (95% CI 93.7 to 98.7), diagnostic yield 79.6% (72.6 to 85.2) and accuracy 82.8% (77.8 to 86.8).
opts.avoid: The superiority claim does not survive the full text. The accuracy odds ratio of 8.69 (1.12 to 67.12) rests on two retrospective unblinded within-patient comparisons, one of them a conference abstract, and the meta-analysis's own results section states there was no significant difference in diagnostic accuracy between forceps and FNA — contradicting its abstract. The yield odds ratio of 4.79 (1.52 to 15.06) has an I-squared of 87%, so there is no single effect to pool, and the prediction interval around the pooled 79.6% yield runs from 4.07% to 97.24%, which predicts nothing about the next series. Serious adverse events were 1.08% (0.43 to 2.69) — one event among 425 procedures, so the interval is a property of the pooling method and not a bound on the hazard — with post-procedure pancreatitis 3.94% (2.36 to 6.48) and bleeding 3.61% (1.38 to 9.09) in a population with a mean cyst size of 33 mm. Ten of the 11 studies were retrospective, two were abstracts, and three scored below the review's own stated quality threshold.

opts.name: Needle-based confocal laser endomicroscopy
opts.when: In situ imaging of the cyst epithelium through the FNA needle. Not in Kyoto's, ACG's or AGA's algorithms, and the European guideline recommends against its use for differential diagnosis at GRADE 1C, citing adverse event rates of 7 to 9% — a strong recommendation on thin evidence, but a recommendation against, which the page previously did not record.
opts.pref: Only at a centre with trained operators and a structured training programme. After a formal training intervention, 21 nCLE-naive early-career endosonographers read 80 video clips with 89% accuracy (95% CI 87 to 90) for mucinous versus non-mucinous and interobserver agreement of kappa 0.63 (0.55 to 0.70); 16 of 21 (76%) reached the study's competency definition at a median of 38 assessments (range 9 to 67).
opts.avoid: The subtype figures are the ones that matter and they are weak in the direction that defeats the purpose. Sensitivity was 57% for mucinous cystic neoplasm, 65% for serous cystadenoma and 73% for cystic neuroendocrine or solid pseudopapillary neoplasm, with interobserver agreement of kappa 0.32 for mucinous cystic neoplasm and 0.44 for serous cystadenoma — so a trained reader misses a third of the serous cystadenomas whose recognition is the economic case for the technique, and two trained readers do not reliably agree. The study measured reading of edited high-yield recorded videos acquired by experts, against a video set engineered to 66% mucinous prevalence, with the same 80 videos used for training and for the retest; five readers never reached competency and remain inside the pooled 89%. It gives no training in performing the examination and no evidence that the technique changes management or survival.

alt.order: Ordered by how firmly the guidelines support them: aspiration is in all four algorithms, microforceps biopsy is in none, and confocal endomicroscopy is recommended against by one. The order reflects guideline standing, not a comparison — no study compares these three against each other, and none reports patient outcomes.
alt.flagnote: Ratification item: whether through-the-needle biopsy and confocal endomicroscopy are offered here at all, and if so under what indication and with what registry capture. Both add cost and a procedural risk to a decision that four guidelines think can be made without them, the forceps superiority claim is contradicted by its own meta-analysis text, and the European guideline recommends against confocal endomicroscopy outright. Audit: use by indication, adverse events, and whether the result changed the plan.

alt.t: Measure serum CA 19-9, and read it as a rule-in test with a stated sensitivity rather than as a screen.
alt.pref: Kyoto 2024 lists an elevated serum CA 19-9 among the worrisome features and does give numbers: above 37 U/L it has 41 to 74% sensitivity and 85 to 96% specificity for invasive carcinoma. The European guideline makes a level above 37 U/mL a relative indication for surgery and reports a positive predictive value of 74.0% with accuracy 81.7% for invasive IPMN. In the Tokyo cohort CA 19-9 above 37 U/mL was independently associated with carcinoma found within 6 months (multivariable odds ratio 6.90, 95% CI 2.08 to 22.9) but was not one of the features that predicted long-term incidence.
alt.avoid: Do not use it to exclude anything — at 41% sensitivity at the low end of Kyoto's range, a normal value means little — and do not act on a single raised value in a jaundiced or cholangitic patient. Fukuoka 2017 adopted the 37 U/L threshold while describing it in the same paragraph as having low specificity.
alt.note: Corrected after the full-text read: the page previously said no guideline gives operating characteristics for CA 19-9. Kyoto 2024 and the European guideline both do. The other systemic worrisome feature, new-onset or worsening diabetes, is new in Kyoto 2024 and is worth asking about directly since it will not appear on the scan — Kyoto reports it in 25% of IPMN patients with a risk ratio of 1.27 for high-grade dysplasia and 1.61 for invasive carcinoma, and states in the same passage that the definitions of 'new onset' and 'acute exacerbation' have not been determined. ACG pairs new or worsening diabetes with growth over 3 mm per year as a trigger for a short-interval study.

avoid.t: Do not read one worrisome feature as an indication to operate.
avoid.pref: Use the count, the trajectory and the patient's fitness. A single feature carried a non-significant subdistribution hazard ratio of 1.43 (95% CI 0.93 to 2.19) in the Tokyo cohort.
avoid.avoid: In 281 patients with worrisome features or high-risk stigmata who were not operated on, 5-year disease-specific survival in the worrisome-feature group was 96.2%, against 60.2% with a high-risk stigma, and the authors concluded that conservative management is appropriate for elderly patients whose IPMN has worrisome features. Read that 96.2% with its construction. The cohort was selected for being unfit or unwilling; 38 patients (13.5%) crossed over to surgery and were kept in the non-operative analysis, 10 of the 36 resected having high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma, so the figure describes a cohort partly rescued by resection; 32 of the 57 deaths were from other causes and the Kaplan-Meier estimate ignores that competing risk; and the lesion itself progressed in 147 of 281 (52%) at a median of 32 months against a median follow-up of 51 months, so 'low progression' in the title means progression to invasive cancer (12%), not stability.
avoid.note: The same paper's figures for the resected minority are the other half of the result and are rarely quoted: postoperative mortality was 8% among the 36 patients resected during follow-up, and all three deaths were in patients whose final pathology showed non-invasive IPMN. It is the best available estimate of what happens when worrisome features are observed, and it does not support operating on one feature — nor does it establish long-term safety.

avoid.t: Do not aspirate a cyst when the result cannot change the plan.
avoid.pref: Decide in advance what a mucinous result, a non-mucinous result and a non-diagnostic result would each change. If the answer is nothing, the patient needs an interval, not a needle.
avoid.avoid: Kyoto 2024 says directly that aspiration should not be performed when a high-risk stigma is obvious and surgery will follow regardless. The same logic applies at the other end: do not aspirate a 12 mm stable cyst in an 84-year-old who would not be operated on whatever came back.

gates.name: 4 · Cyst fluid, and when molecular testing earns its place
crit: Enough fluid aspirated to allocate between chemistry, cytology and molecular testing before any tube is sent
The question the aspirate is meant to answer stated first — is it mucinous, or does it harbour advanced neoplasia?
Glucose and CEA on the same specimen where volume allows
Cytology sent in every case
Molecular panel sent only where the result would change management and where funding is confirmed
gates.ask: What exactly am I asking this fluid, and have I allocated the volume to answer it?

opts.name: Cyst fluid glucose
opts.when: The best-performing single chemistry test for mucinous versus non-mucinous, and the one Kyoto 2024 quotes first: glucose below 50 mg/dL, 93% sensitivity and 89% specificity (SIGN evidence 1+, grade B).
opts.pref: First-line on every aspirate where the question is mucinous or not. Two meta-analyses agree: pooled sensitivity 91% (95% CI 88 to 94) and specificity 86% (81 to 90) in 8 studies and 609 lesions, and 90.5% (88.1 to 92.5) and 88.0% (80.8 to 92.7) in 7 studies and 566 patients. At a 50 mg/dL cut-off, sensitivity 90.1% (87.2 to 92.5) and specificity 85.3% (76.8 to 91.1). It can be run on a point-of-care glucometer (sensitivity 89.5%, specificity 83.9%, 68.5 to 92.6) on under 2 microlitres, against 50 for laboratory glucose and 200 for CEA.
opts.avoid: It says nothing about grade. A low glucose identifies a mucinous cyst, not a dangerous one, and the entire resection decision at gates 2 and 3 is about grade. Pseudocysts also have low intracystic glucose and were handled differently across the contributing studies, so part of the apparent discrimination against 'non-mucinous' lesions depends on how many collections each cohort contained.

opts.name: Cyst fluid CEA
opts.when: The historical standard, from the cooperative pancreatic cyst study: a cut-off of 192 ng/mL gave the largest area under the curve (0.79) with sensitivity 75.0% (42 of 56), specificity 83.6% (46 of 55) and accuracy 79.2% (88 of 111), against 50.9% for EUS morphology and 58.7% for cytology.
opts.pref: Alongside glucose where volume allows, and as the fallback where glucose is unavailable. It is specific: ACG quotes pooled sensitivity 63% (59 to 67) with specificity 93% (90 to 95); Kyoto quotes 58% and 87%; the European guideline quotes 52 to 78% and 63 to 91%.
opts.avoid: Insensitive, and it does not grade. In the head-to-head meta-analysis CEA's pooled sensitivity was 56% (46 to 66) against glucose's 91%, and overall accuracy 85% against 94% (P<.001); adding CEA to glucose did not improve on glucose alone. Kyoto 2024 adds that up to 30% of IPMNs have a low cyst fluid CEA, that it does not distinguish IPMN from mucinous cystic neoplasm, and that it does not correlate with dysplasia grade. It also consumes four times the volume glucose does.

opts.name: Cyst fluid amylase
opts.when: Used for one question only: is this a pseudocyst? Amylase below 250 U/L gave pooled sensitivity 44% and specificity 98% in 12 studies and 450 patients, with amylase values available in 155 of them, and the European guideline quotes the same figures.
opts.pref: The patient in whom a history of pancreatitis makes a collection a real possibility. A low amylase effectively excludes it; median amylase in the pooled series was 11,000 U/L in pseudocysts against 250 in serous and 8,000 in mucinous cystadenomas.
opts.avoid: Do not use it to separate mucinous from non-mucinous neoplasms — it does not. Because sensitivity is 44%, a high amylase does not establish a pseudocyst either; branch-duct IPMNs communicate with the duct and can have amylase in the thousands. And note where the figures come from: the pooled analysis excluded IPMN entirely, so the test was never characterised in the commonest neoplastic cyst, and the 250 U/L line was chosen to maximise classification within the same data that report it.

opts.name: Cytology
opts.when: ACG states that cyst fluid cytology should be sent to assess for high-grade dysplasia. This is the one fluid test that speaks to grade, and grade is what the operation is for.
opts.pref: Every aspirate. A suspicious or positive cytology is itself a high-risk stigma in Kyoto 2024 and an absolute indication for surgery in the European guideline, and the rule-in value is strong: Kyoto puts the absolute risk of high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma at 91 to 100% for a suspicious and 100% for a positive result by the WHO criteria.
opts.avoid: Insensitive, and therefore not reassuring when negative. Kyoto 2024's own pooled sensitivity for EUS-FNA cyst fluid cytology is 28.7% (range 4.8 to 61.5%). ACG quotes pooled sensitivity 54 to 63% with specificity 88 to 93%, and for cancer specifically 64.8% sensitivity with 90.6% specificity; the European guideline quotes 42% sensitivity and 99% specificity for mucinous versus non-mucinous, and 27 to 48% sensitivity with 83 to 100% specificity overall; the pooled individual-patient analysis found malignant cells in 53 of 111 mucinous cystadenocarcinomas (48%); and in the cooperative cyst study cytology identified malignancy within a malignant mucinous cyst in 7 of 32 cases (22%). A negative cytology excludes nothing.

opts.name: Targeted next-generation sequencing of cyst fluid
opts.when: Not required by any of the four guidelines, but the best-evidenced addition since Fukuoka 2017. Kyoto 2024 devotes a section to it and gives its molecular recommendations the highest evidence level in the whole document (1+, grade B); ACG says molecular markers are early in development with insufficient evidence for routine use; the European guideline says KRAS and GNAS testing may be considered at GRADE 2C when the diagnosis is unclear and a change would alter management.
opts.pref: Where the cyst type is genuinely unresolved, or where a result indicating advanced neoplasia would move a borderline patient to theatre. In a prospective study of specimens from 31 institutions, 1,887 of 1,933 (98%) were adequate: MAPK-pathway or GNAS mutations gave 90% sensitivity and 100% specificity for a mucinous cyst (PPV 100%, NPV 77%), against 77% and 92% for increased fluid viscosity and 73% and 94% for CEA above 192 ng/mL. Adding TP53, SMAD4 or mTOR-pathway alterations at allele frequencies equal to the driver gave 87% sensitivity and 99% specificity for advanced neoplasia (PPV 98%, NPV 92%), rising to 89% and 98% with CTNNB1 (PPV 97%, NPV 93%) and to 93% sensitivity at 95% specificity with cytology added. VHL alterations identified serous cystadenomas (71% sensitivity, 100% specificity) and MEN1 with loss of heterozygosity of TP53, SMAD4, PTEN or RNF43 identified cystic neuroendocrine tumours (68%, 98%; MEN1 alone, 27% and 100%).
opts.avoid: Read the limits honestly, and do not apply the headline figure to the cyst in front of you without checking which lesion it came from. KRAS, BRAF or GNAS alterations were found in 159 of 167 IPMNs (95%) but KRAS in only 9 of 19 mucinous cystic neoplasms (47%), so for a non-communicating body or tail cyst in a middle-aged woman the sensitivity is 47%, not 90%. Surgical pathology existed for only 251 of 1,832 tested patients (14%), or 251 of the 1,216 with follow-up (21%), so the performance figures rest on the operated minority, and the decision to operate was itself informed by the molecular result — which depresses the measured sensitivity of the comparator criteria and inflates that of the panel. The allele-frequency rules that lift specificity to 98 to 100% were derived in the same group's earlier single-centre cohorts and the confirmation cohort came from the same molecular archive, and every specimen was processed in the one lead laboratory, so 'multi-institutional' describes where the fluid came from and not where it was analysed. The panel is that laboratory's assay rather than a class of test, charged at $750 per specimen in the 2018 series, so another laboratory's panel does not inherit these numbers. Kyoto 2024's own pooled figures for the grade markers are much weaker — TP53, SMAD4, CDKN2A and PIK3CA alterations at 9 to 39% sensitivity and 92 to 98% specificity — so a negative molecular result is not a reason to stand down. Nine resected IPMNs were driver-negative preoperatively and positive on the specimen, which makes the 90% sensitivity partly a property of the aspiration rather than of the sequencing. Coverage must be confirmed in writing before this enters routine practice. [PAYER]

standard.order: Ordered by how much of the aspirate each one needs and how early it answers something useful, not by any comparative trial of testing strategies — none exists. Glucose comes first because it is the cheapest, needs the least fluid and outperformed CEA head to head; cytology is in the list regardless of volume because it is the only one of the five that speaks to grade.
standard.flagnote: Two ratification items. First, whether glucose replaces CEA as the first-line chemistry here or is added to it: the meta-analytic case for glucose is strong but neither ACG nor the European guideline names it, Kyoto 2024 quotes it without recommending it, and the two meta-analyses pool largely the same seven primary studies, so they are not independent confirmation of each other. Second, whether molecular testing is offered, to whom, and who pays: the prospective multi-institutional data are good, no guideline requires it, it is a single laboratory's assay, and the authors' finding that the AGA and IAP/Fukuoka algorithms performed worse than the panel was reached by reconstructing those guidelines retrospectively from records submitted by 31 sites with unstandardised EUS and local cytology while the panel ran prospectively in one accredited laboratory. Audit: tests sent per aspirate, non-diagnostic rate, and whether each result changed the recorded plan.

alt.t: Where volume is limited, send glucose and cytology and accept that CEA will be missing.
alt.pref: The small cyst that yields under a millilitre — which is common. Glucose on a glucometer needs under 2 microlitres, cytology is the only test that addresses grade, and in the pooled analysis the combination of low glucose or raised CEA was no better than glucose alone on overlapping intervals.
alt.avoid: Do not sacrifice cytology to get a chemistry panel. A mucinous-versus-non-mucinous answer without a grade answer does not change the resection decision at gates 2 and 3. And note what the combination actually costs: pooled accuracy was 97% (95 to 98) against 94% (91 to 96) for glucose alone, but specificity fell from 86% to 72% (47 to 88) with an I-squared of 69%, so adding CEA to glucose buys sensitivity by giving up specificity in a population where most cysts are benign.
alt.note: Agree the allocation order with the endoscopy and pathology services in advance, not in the room. Sample adequacy is the real constraint: in the two large molecular series, 59 to 60% of specimens were less than optimal or unsatisfactory for cytology and fluid was insufficient for CEA in 23 to 28%.

avoid.t: Do not use cyst fluid CEA to grade dysplasia.
avoid.pref: Use cytology for grade, and the molecular grade markers only with their weak sensitivity stated.
avoid.avoid: ACG states plainly that CEA cannot be used to identify IPMNs and MCNs with high-grade dysplasia or pancreatic cancer, and Kyoto 2024 that CEA does not correlate with dysplasia grade. The 192 ng/mL cut-off was selected to maximise correct classification in the same 112 resected cysts in which it was then scored, with no split sample and no external cohort, and only 112 of the 341 enrolled patients (33%) had histological verification — verification that depended on the very findings under test. Mucinous lesions were 60% of that verified cohort and 59% of those were malignant or borderline, far above any cyst clinic's prevalence, and CEA values overlapped widely within the malignant group.
avoid.note: Downgraded to C from B after the full-text read: the threshold is an in-sample optimum in a partially verified surgical subset, which is a C-grade derivation however widely the number is quoted.

avoid.t: Do not treat a negative fluid result as a reason to lengthen an interval or discharge a patient.
avoid.pref: A negative result returns the patient to the interval their size and features already earned them. It does not buy a longer one.
avoid.avoid: Negative predictive value for a mucinous cyst was 77% even on the best-performing molecular panel, cytology missed more than half of mucinous cystadenocarcinomas in the pooled individual-patient analysis and has a 28.7% pooled sensitivity in Kyoto's own figures, and the molecular grade markers have 9 to 39% sensitivity in the same document. Every cut-off on this gate — CEA at 192 ng/mL, amylase at 250 U/L, CEA at 800 ng/mL, the glucose thresholds pooled across 30, 41 and 50 mg/dL, and the allele-frequency rules on the molecular panel — was fitted in the data that report its performance. None of these tests was designed or validated to shorten a surveillance programme.
avoid.note: The one piece of reassurance offered for a negative molecular result is that none of the 965 prospectively tested patients who did not undergo surgery developed malignancy; the median follow-up was 23 months, in a lesion whose dwell time is estimated at 15 to 20 years, so that is an absence of events and not a finding.

gates.name: 5 · Not an IPMN: the other five cysts
crit: Mucinous cystic neoplasm — non-communicating, usually body or tail, ovarian-type stroma on histology
Serous cystadenoma — microcystic or honeycomb, central scar or calcification, no duct communication
Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm — young woman, solid and cystic, often large
Cystic neuroendocrine tumour — enhancing rim, often in a hereditary syndrome
Pseudocyst or walled-off collection — a pancreatitis history, high amylase, no epithelium
gates.ask: If this is not an IPMN, does it still need an operation — because two of these always do and two of them never do?

opts.name: Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm — resect
opts.when: The European guideline states that radical resection should be performed for all solid pseudopapillary neoplasms, and ACG recommends referral to a multidisciplinary group for consideration of resection.
opts.pref: Every patient fit for the operation, at any size. These are malignant neoplasms with a good prognosis after complete resection — ACG reports over 98% 5-year disease-specific survival, with aggressive behaviour in about 10% — and they occur in young patients in whom a surveillance commitment would run for decades.
opts.avoid: There is no surveillance option in any of the four guidelines and no size threshold, so do not construct one. The evidence is observational throughout — no trial has ever randomised this disease — and the preoperative diagnosis was right in only 2 of 4 cases in the Amsterdam resection series. ACG also asks for yearly follow-up for at least 5 years after resection, on a 4.4% recurrence rate at a median of 50.5 months, which the page previously did not record.

opts.name: Mucinous cystic neoplasm — resect, but where is the threshold?
opts.when: This is the clearest disagreement on the page. The European guideline, at GRADE 1B: 'MCN >=40 mm should undergo surgical resection', with resection also for symptomatic lesions or those with a mural nodule at any size, and it is safe at GRADE 2C to follow presumed MCN under 40 mm without risk features. NCCN, summarising the international group, states that resection is recommended for all MCNs in patients who can undergo surgery.
opts.pref: A fit patient with a non-communicating mucinous cyst in the body or tail, where the operation is a distal pancreatectomy. The malignant risk is real but modest and the full-text read narrows it: NCCN puts it below 15%, Fukuoka 2012 reports under 15% invasive carcinoma in series that required ovarian-type stroma and no malignancy at all below 4 cm without mural nodules, ACG reports high-grade dysplasia or cancer in 10% of 90 resected MCNs with no case under 3 cm that had a normal CA 19-9 and no concerning features, and in the Amsterdam series 2 of 14 resected MCNs were malignant (both 65 to 67 mm, one with a nodule) and 1 had high-grade dysplasia (150 mm with a nodule), while the premalignant remainder had a median diameter of 45 mm.
opts.avoid: Do not quote 'always resect' to a frail 80-year-old with a 2 cm tail cyst, and do not quote 'surveil under 40 mm' to a fit 45-year-old, without saying that the other guideline says the opposite. The 'resect all' position has a weak provenance: Sendai 2006 made it on malignancy rates of 6 to 36% from series that largely did not require ovarian-type stroma — which its own text concedes inflates them, the stroma-requiring series giving 6 to 27% — and on the assertion that left pancreatectomy carries low morbidity and practically no mortality, with no pooled estimate offered. Fukuoka 2017 then removed MCN from scope on the stated ground that controversy had subsided rather than that anything had been settled, leaving the 2012 recommendation in force unexamined, and Kyoto 2024 is an IPMN guideline that does not adjudicate it.

opts.name: Cystic neuroendocrine tumour — size decides
opts.when: The European guideline: surgery for cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms over 20 mm; surveillance for asymptomatic lesions of 2 cm or less without signs of malignant behaviour.
opts.pref: Confirm the diagnosis before committing. On fluid molecular testing, MEN1 alteration alone gave 27% sensitivity at 100% specificity and MEN1 with loss of heterozygosity of TP53, SMAD4, PTEN or RNF43 68% at 98%, from 34 resected cystic lesions; cytology gave 85% and 100% and the combination 97% and 98%. Ask about MEN1 and von Hippel-Lindau disease, because in a hereditary syndrome the operation and its timing are different. This is the PNET pathway from here — the grade, the functional status, the 2 cm threshold and the enucleation-versus-resection question belong on that page.
opts.avoid: Do not manage one of these on a cyst interval schedule; the surveillance logic for a neuroendocrine tumour is grade-driven and is not IPMN logic. And do not lean on the molecular numbers for the 2 cm decision: the prognostic loss-of-heterozygosity analysis that reported 83% sensitivity for distant metastasis pooled 34 cystic lesions with 53 solid biopsies, a different presentation, and the preoperative diagnosis of a neuroendocrine tumour was correct in only 1 of 3 cases in the Amsterdam resection series.

opts.name: Serous cystadenoma — do not resect for size
opts.when: The European guideline calls it a benign entity with essentially no deaths attributable to malignant behaviour and recommends follow-up for 1 year after a radiological diagnosis, then symptom-based follow-up only. ACG states that resected serous cystadenomas require no further follow-up.
opts.pref: Confident imaging diagnosis plus, where doubt remains, fluid testing — VHL alterations without KRAS or GNAS identified serous cystadenomas with 71% sensitivity and 100% specificity in the prospective multi-institutional series, from 13 resected cases, and Kyoto 2024 reports VHL mutation without KRAS or GNAS at over 99% sensitivity in its own pooling.
opts.avoid: Operate only for an uncertain diagnosis after full workup, for genuine related symptoms, or exceptionally for a real concern about malignancy. In 2,622 patients across 71 centres there were 3 serous cystadenocarcinomas (0.1%), all in symptomatic patients with lesions of 71 to 170 mm, and 1 disease-related death among the 1,032 never operated (0.1%), against a reported postoperative mortality of 10 of 1,590 operated patients (0.6%).

opts.name: Pseudocyst or walled-off collection — not an oncological problem
opts.when: A pancreatitis, alcohol or trauma history with a cyst fluid amylase above 250 U/L and no epithelium. Amylase below 250 U/L effectively excludes it (sensitivity 44%, specificity 98%).
opts.pref: Treat on symptoms — infection, obstruction, pain — not on size, and off this page entirely. ACG states that a drained pseudocyst needs no further follow-up.
opts.avoid: The dangerous error is the reverse one and it is well documented: a mucinous neoplasm labelled a pseudocyst and drained. In one series of 134 symptomatic cysts, 44% of the patients who presented with pancreatitis and had a neoplastic cyst were initially misdiagnosed as having a pseudocyst. Satisfy yourself that there is a pancreatitis history before accepting the label, and remember that the amylase figures come from a pooled analysis that excluded IPMN.

standard.order: Ordered from 'always resect' to 'never resect for size', which is the order a surgeon needs in the room. The order reflects guideline wording and observational series only; no comparative study ranks management of these entities, the serous cystadenoma position rests on a single large retrospective multinational cohort, and the solid pseudopapillary position rests on no cohort at all.
standard.flagnote: Ratification item, and the sharpest one on this page: does this programme resect every mucinous cystic neoplasm in a fit patient, as NCCN's summary of the international group says, or surveil those under 40 mm without risk features, as the European evidence-based guideline says? The two positions differ by a large number of distal pancreatectomies a year. The full-text read moves the balance toward the European position — no malignancy below 4 cm without nodules in the stroma-defined series Fukuoka 2012 cites, 10% high-grade dysplasia or cancer in 90 resected MCNs with none under 3 cm, and in the one series that reports resected MCNs individually the three with advanced disease were 65, 67 and 150 mm — but the 'resect all' position is held by serious people and rests on the difficulty of identifying invasion before the operation. Decide also whether the threshold varies with age. Audit: MCNs by size, management chosen, and final histology in every resected case.

alt.t: Where the entity cannot be settled on imaging and the management forks on it, aspirate for the discriminating test rather than committing to either path.
alt.pref: The classic unresolved pair — a macrocystic serous cystadenoma against a mucinous cystic neoplasm, or a cystic neuroendocrine tumour against either. Glucose and CEA separate mucinous from non-mucinous; VHL and MEN1 patterns on a molecular panel identify serous and neuroendocrine lesions specifically; amylase rules in a collection.
alt.avoid: Do not aspirate when the plan is the same either way. In 115 resections the preoperative diagnosis was wrong in 32 (28%), and for the entities on this gate it was worse: serous cystic neoplasm 33.3% correct, neuroendocrine tumour 33.3%, solid pseudopapillary neoplasm 50.0%, against 92.9% for mucinous cystic neoplasm. The honest statement to the patient is that the operation may also be the diagnostic test.
alt.note: Kyoto 2024 is an IPMN guideline and says almost nothing about these entities beyond the cyst-fluid markers. The non-IPMN recommendations on this page come from the European 2018 guideline and ACG 2018, which is why they carry grade C at best, and the molecular figures for serous and neuroendocrine lesions rest on 13 and 34 resected cases respectively.

avoid.t: Do not resect a confidently diagnosed serous cystadenoma because it is large or because it grew.
avoid.pref: Size and slow growth are the natural history of the entity. Among 1,271 patients followed beyond a year the lesion was stable in 724 (57%), grew in 476 (37%) and shrank in 71 (6%, mostly after aspiration); the median growth rate was 4 mm per year in those eventually operated and 1 mm per year in those never operated (P<0.001), and 104 of 963 asymptomatic patients (11%) became symptomatic.
avoid.avoid: In that series 1,351 of 2,622 patients (52%) were operated within a year of diagnosis and the commonest surgical indication, in 950 of 1,590 operated cases (60%), was diagnostic uncertainty rather than any feature of the lesion — and among those, only 13% had all three of CT, MRI and EUS, 47% had CT alone, and aspiration accompanied EUS in only 30%. That is the overtreatment pattern to avoid, and it is avoidable by completing the work-up.
avoid.note: The two mortality figures on either side of this argument have different denominators and are not exchangeable: one disease-related death among the 1,032 patients never operated (0.1%), ten postoperative deaths among the 1,590 operated (0.6%), and the operated cysts were larger (40 against 25 mm) and more often symptomatic. The authors also state that their operative mortality is self-reported and probably lower than the 1 to 3% of high-volume centres, and that 785 patients (30%) were diagnosed radiologically only, in a disease where blinded CT and MRI accuracy for serous cystadenoma has been reported as low as 27%. The 0.1% malignancy rate also counts only distant metastasis per the WHO definition; 18 further lesions were called locally aggressive and set aside, 14 of them from a single centre.

avoid.t: Do not place a mucinous cystic neoplasm or a cystic neoplasm of unknown type on a drainage pathway.
avoid.pref: Establish that there is a pancreatitis history and a high amylase before anyone passes a stent or a drain.
avoid.avoid: Drainage of a mucinous neoplasm mistaken for a collection converts a resectable premalignant lesion into a contaminated, inflamed field, and forfeits the clean distal pancreatectomy that would have been curative. The misdiagnosis is common in exactly this direction: 44% of patients with a neoplastic cyst presenting with pancreatitis were first called pseudocysts in one series of 134.
avoid.note: Grade D: no study quantifies the harm of drainage in this situation, and none will. The recommendation rests on the mechanism and on the documented frequency of the misdiagnosis.

gates.name: 6 · Who should not be operated on
crit: Fitness for the specific operation the lesion's position requires, assessed before any threshold is quoted
Life expectancy from competing causes estimated and written down alongside the cyst's risk
Age, comorbidity and the patient's own preference recorded, as Kyoto 2024 requires
The operation's own morbidity and mortality quoted to the patient in numbers
A high-volume pancreatic service available to do it
gates.ask: This cyst crosses a threshold — but will this operation shorten this patient's life rather than lengthen it?

standard.t: Weigh the cyst's risk against the patient's competing risk of death, in numbers, and record both.
standard.pref: Every patient over about 70, and every patient with significant cardiorespiratory, renal or oncological comorbidity. The competing risk is usually the larger number: among 1,617 patients whose presumed branch-duct IPMN stayed free of worrisome features and high-risk stigmata for at least 5 years, all-cause mortality was 4.9% (79 patients) and disease-specific mortality 0.3% (5 patients) — about sixteen deaths from something else for every death from the cyst. ACG cites the same pattern from two cohorts: of 725 IPMN patients, 24% died at a median of 5 years with 78% of the deaths unrelated to the IPMN, and a Charlson-age index of 7 or more carried an eleven-fold higher chance of non-IPMN death within 3 years.
standard.avoid: Do not present the competing-risk argument as a reason never to operate on an older patient. In the non-operated multicentre cohort with a high-risk stigma, 5-year disease-specific survival was 60.2%, so the cyst does kill people; the argument is about which patients, not about whether.
standard.note: Kyoto 2024 requires exactly this weighing — general condition, comorbidity, life expectancy and preference — in every operative decision, including decisions driven by a high-risk stigma, and adds that surveillance should be discontinued in patients with a life expectancy under 10 years. Comorbidity is not static: in the 1,617-patient cohort the proportion with an age-adjusted Charlson index of 7 or more rose from 18% at diagnosis to 24% by 5 years, so a fitness judgement made at enrolment expires.

standard.t: Quote the operation's own numbers, not just the cyst's, because the guidelines that set the thresholds do not state them.
standard.pref: Every consent conversation for a cyst resection. The published figures that exist: for cyst resection generally, 2.1% mortality with 30% morbidity (ACG) and 2% mortality with 30% major morbidity in centres of excellence against 6.6% across all US pancreatic surgery in SEER (AGA); in the 164 resections generated by the largest branch-duct surveillance cohort, major morbidity 17.1% and 30-day mortality 2.4% (4 patients); in 412 resected IPMNs at one high-volume centre, major complications 15.2%, pancreatic fistula of any grade 13.5%, 30-day mortality 0.9%; for total pancreatectomy, 25% major morbidity and 6% 30-day mortality (95% CI 4 to 8%) across 52 studies and 3,570 patients, with exocrine insufficiency symptoms in 33% and hypoglycaemia-related mortality in 10 of 568 (1.8%); and in the international serous cystadenoma series a reported postoperative mortality of 0.6% against a disease-specific mortality of 0.1%.
standard.avoid: Do not use benchmark figures from another centre. The number the patient needs is this programme's own 90-day mortality and major morbidity for this operation, which is why it is a dashboard metric and an approvals item. And note the direction of the bias in the published numbers: the serous cystadenoma figure is self-reported and its authors say it is probably an underestimate, and the PROPAN decision tables tell patients that 2 to 5 of 100 will die of operative complications in very high-volume centres while the same paper's own pooled estimate across 3,570 patients was 6%.
standard.note: [EXPERTISE] These are elective operations on patients who are, in the main, well, so the threshold for accepting a complication is lower than it is in pancreatic adenocarcinoma. It is worth saying plainly where these numbers had to come from: Sendai 2006, Fukuoka 2012, Fukuoka 2017, Kyoto 2024 and the European 2018 guideline quantify surgical mortality and morbidity nowhere in their texts, so every resection threshold in the spine of this page is stated with the risk of not operating in numbers and the risk of operating not stated at all.

standard.t: Stop the surveillance conversation entirely in a patient who would not be operated on whatever the imaging showed.
standard.pref: This is the one point on which all four guidelines agree. ACG makes discontinuation when a patient is no longer a surgical candidate a strong recommendation; the European guideline follows patients 'until they are no longer fit for surgery'; AGA 2015 names loss of surgical candidacy as a stopping condition and adds that surveillance is inappropriate from the outset for patients with limited life expectancy; Kyoto 2024 asks for life expectancy to be considered and says surveillance should be discontinued below a 10-year expectancy.
standard.avoid: Do not carry a patient on a surveillance list out of inertia. An interval scan in someone who would never have the operation generates anxiety, incidental findings and cost, and cannot change anything — and up to 30% of patients under cyst surveillance report difficulty sleeping and find it burdensome.
standard.note: Grade D: this is a logical requirement, not a comparative result. No study has randomised stopping against continuing in anyone. It is also the only one of the four guidelines' stopping statements that is strongly recommended on any evidence grade, and ACG grades even this one on very low quality evidence.

opts.name: Resect
opts.when: A high-risk stigma or several worrisome features in a patient whose competing-risk estimate is long enough for the cyst to matter.
opts.pref: Younger and fitter patients, where a decades-long surveillance commitment is itself a cost, and where a high-risk stigma was accompanied by prevalent carcinoma in 49% of cases in the Tokyo cohort.
opts.avoid: That 49% is a prevalence at the moment the stigma was found, in a design where the stigma triggered the work-up, so it is not a forecast. Do not operate to resolve diagnostic uncertainty in an elderly patient: that is the documented overtreatment pattern, diagnostic uncertainty having been the indication in 60% of serous cystadenoma resections in the international series, and in the Amsterdam series 54.8% of cyst resections removed a lesion with neither high-grade dysplasia nor malignancy.

opts.name: Continue surveillance despite the feature
opts.when: Kyoto 2024 permits it implicitly by making the operative decision conditional on condition, comorbidity, life expectancy and preference; the European guideline follows patients while they remain fit for surgery and recommends 6-monthly imaging specifically for the elderly, the comorbid and those with relative indications.
opts.pref: The elderly or comorbid patient with worrisome features but no high-risk stigma, where 5-year disease-specific survival without operation was 96.2% in the non-operated multicentre cohort and the authors concluded that conservative management is appropriate.
opts.avoid: Weaker ground with a high-risk stigma, where disease-specific survival without operation was 60.2% and fell to 0% at 5 years with two or more stigmata. Read the 96.2% with its caveats — the cohort was selected for being unfit or unwilling, 13.5% crossed over to surgery and stayed in the analysis, competing risks are ignored in the estimate and the lesion progressed in 52% at a median of 32 months. Document that the patient was offered the operation and declined it, or that it was judged unsafe, and name who made that judgement.

opts.name: Stop surveillance and treat symptoms only
opts.when: All four guidelines when surgical candidacy is gone.
opts.pref: Severe comorbidity, limited life expectancy, or a patient who has decided they will not have the operation under any circumstances. Say it plainly and record it. Gardner's review adds the cases in which stopping is uncontroversial: a confirmed serous cystic neoplasm or other benign cyst on aspiration or biopsy, multiple comorbidities on a standard index, medical unfitness for surgery, and a patient aligned with a palliative philosophy.
opts.avoid: Do not slide into this by letting intervals lapse. A decision to stop is a decision, and it needs a conversation and a note.

alt.order: Ordered as the decision is usually met, from the most interventional to the least. The order carries no survival claim: there is no randomised comparison of resection against surveillance for any pancreatic cystic neoplasm, long-term prospective comparative studies of observation against resection do not exist, and the cohorts that compare them are selected in favour of surveillance because the frailer patients were not operated on.
alt.flagnote: Ratification item: whether this programme sets an age or fitness rule for entering surveillance at all — for example, not opening a surveillance programme on a small cyst without worrisome features in a patient over a stated age or above a stated comorbidity burden. The standardised incidence ratios from the 12-centre cohort suggest the cyst adds nothing to background risk in exactly that group (1.12, 95% CI 0.23 to 3.39 in patients 75 or older after 5 years of stability, from 3 cancers), but no guideline states an entry rule, AGA 2015 comes closest by calling surveillance inappropriate where life expectancy is limited, and inventing a local rule is a governance decision rather than an evidence one. Audit: new surveillance enrolments by age and cyst size, and reason for enrolment.

avoid.t: Do not count the proportion of cyst resections that turned out to be justified as a success rate until you have measured it here.
avoid.pref: Audit it. In 115 consecutive pancreatic cyst resections at one centre, surgery was justified in retrospect in 52 patients (45.2%) — malignancy in 35, high-grade dysplasia in 6, solid pseudopapillary neoplasm in 4, neuroendocrine tumour in 3 and symptom relief in 4 — and resection relieved symptoms in only 2 of the 4 patients operated for a symptomatic lesion.
avoid.avoid: That means 63 of 115 resections (54.8%) removed a lesion that did not need removing — a premalignant cyst without high-grade dysplasia or malignancy in 40.8% and a cyst with no malignant potential in 13.9% — in an operation with real mortality. Any programme that does not know its own figure is assuming it is better than published. In the same cohort 22 patients (19.1%) had died at a median of 15 months after surgery, with no 30-day deaths, and that mortality is nowhere related to pathology or indication.
avoid.note: Read the benchmark with its construction before adopting it as a target. 'Justified' is the authors' own composite and counts any neuroendocrine tumour, any solid pseudopapillary neoplasm and any symptom improvement, none of which is an endpoint any of the four guidelines was designed to hit, so 45% is not strictly a guideline performance figure. The three-guideline comparison in the same paper is structurally one-sided: the cohort was selected for resection by the IAP and European criteria, so those two cannot be measured as missing anything, while the AGA criteria are scored on a population they never selected. Applying AGA strictly would have avoided 21 of 75 resections (28%) against 8 (11%) for IAP and 7 (9%) for the European guideline, but would have missed 4 of 33 patients (12%) with high-grade dysplasia or malignancy against none missed by the other two — and those 4 are two lesions, a 15 mm main-duct IPMN and a 23 mm side-branch IPMN with a nodule, each counted once as malignant and once as high-grade dysplasia.
